Dataset_Description:
This file contains unfrozen water content data as measured by Al Tice using his nmr technique.  The data is in the following format:
line 1:
   Soil, Test type
line 2:
   Wet density [g/cc], dry density [g/cc], gravimetric water content [g water/g soil],
   volumetric water content [cc water/cc total]
line 3 till next soil:
   temperature [-C], gravimetric unfrozen water content [g unfrozen water/g soil]
Dataset_Notes:
Volume-mass properties were underdefined. A specific gravity of 2.65 was assumed for all soils to complete volume-mass information.
Zero experimental values of Temperature and water content were removed during import
Grainsize curves were used to predict soil-water characteristic curves. The SWCC's were then used to do preliminary modelling and conceptual design of a tailings pond cover.

Dataset_Description: Physical Characteristics of Soils in the Southern Region: Cecil
Dataset_Notes:
Physical Characteristics of Soils in the Southern Region
Cecil
R. R. Bruce, J. H. Dane,
V. L. Quisenberry, N. L. Powell,
and A. W. Thomas


Introduction

As levels of soil management are intensified to achieve greater crop production, while preserving the soil resource, a more complete characterization of the soil physical system is required.  Characteristics associated with describing soil water and solute transport as well as soil water retention are particularly important if water supplied by irrigation and rainfall is to be used effectively.  Soil water potential and hydraulic conductivity as functions of water content are critical to such characterization.
The data reported in this bulletin were obtained from plots in Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina, and Virginia on sites classified as Cecil.  The Cecil series is classified as being in the clayey, kaolinitic, thermic family of Typic Hapludults.  The field and laboratory procedures and measurements that were used are not identical from location to location, but they do have several important measurements in common where procedures were similar.  Therefore, the data can be used to assess the variability of these

physical characteristics within the soil series.  In some instances, there are sufficient measurements to assess within pedons the variability of selected physical quantities.  The data also provide an opportunity to compare in situ measurements with laboratory measurements on undisturbed core samples or other samples.  Although this report does not attempt to proceed very far with an analysis of the data, it provides a unique reservoir of data for a variety of uses.
These data were the result of studies conducted in the years 1977 to 198 1, inclusive, and contributed to regional project S-124, entitled "Movement and retention of water and solutes in selected southern region field soils." The S-124 Technical Committee was composed, for the most part, of trained and experienced soil physicists associated with universities, state agricultural experiment stations, and federal agencies in the southern region.
